newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle $67 sales fade late - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle $67 sales fade late - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle Wednesday sold at $67.00 per cwt in active trade, unchanged from last week, feedlot sources said.
Sales slowed late in the afternoon as packers pulled bids back to $66.00, they said.
Packers reportedly pulled bids back in response to ongoing weakness in beef prices at midday, makret sources said.
About 40,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and about 28,000 in Kansas before owners started passing on the reduced bids, livestock dealers said.
"I guess they sensed they didn't have to pay $67.00 anymore, but I doubt they got all they needed," one Panhandle feedlot manager said.

Beef prices at midday were quoted down $0.45 to $0.69 per cwt, with 213 loads of fabricated beef sold, USDA reported. Heavier-weight choice beef was quoted down $0.45 at $101.19, the lowest since February 21, USDA statistics showed.
The heavyweight choice beef value has dropped $3.02 since prices started their latest decline a week ago on Wednesday.
Beef weakness was tied to belief that retailers had enough orders booked to cover mid-month promotion needs, they said.
